name: slogprobe
description:
THE BANK-0 STACK HINT MUST COVER LIBC, and syslog(3) is the path that showed it did not.  apple/fgx#404.

stack_measure builds its call graph from the program's OWN .s and drops every edge whose callee it cannot see, on the reasoning that those are `_fcc_*' helpers with a register ABI.  libc is not: syslog reaches fprintf reaches __lc_vpf, each pushing a return address and its arguments onto the same bank-0 stack.  /sbin/reboot was sized at 2 pages -- 512 bytes -- and this probe measures 526 through the same three calls.

WHAT IT ASSERTS: the syslog line comes out INTACT, read back from /usr/adm/messages, where syslogd(8) writes it.  `reboot: -; rebooted by root' is what reboot(8) logs, and the reported symptom was that line with characters replaced -- `D-Fm>t: -; rebooted by rootD8m<'.  A stack that overruns its reservation writes into whatever is below it, and strings are what that looks like.  The probe waits up to 20 s for a line past the file's size at the call that carries the text EXACTLY, and prints `SPLINE found:' only then, so a corrupted line, a syslogd that is not running and a datagram that never reached it all fail the same needle.  The console shows the line too -- the conf sends *.crit there -- which is why the needle is SPLINE's and not the text alone.

SP lines report stksize against stkhwm from procinfo, so a future under-size is visible in the transcript rather than only in its consequences.

THEN logger(1), through the same daemon and file.  `LGT: a%sb x y' is the line grep reads back, and the typed command cannot supply it: the command has `-t LGT' and a quoted `'a%sb'', never `LGT:' with a colon, which syslog(3) adds after the tag.  Each part is a defect 2.11BSD's logger had: the `%s' survives only because the text goes through "%s" rather than being the format; the words are joined by the loop that replaced the unbounded strcat; and `-p user.notice' goes through pencode and both brace-elided name tables, where a wrong row layout answers `unknown priority name' and logs nothing.

AND A MESSAGE LONGER THAN syslog(3)'s 640-BYTE LINE IS CUT AT IT.  `SP bigline x=610' is 637 bytes of room (two kept for LOG_CONS's "\r\n") less the 27-byte `<13>Mon dd hh:mm:ss SPBIG: ' head.  MEASURED THE OTHER WAY: with 2.11BSD's unbounded vsprintf the message runs past tbuf into fmt_cpy, the format vsprintf is still reading, so it reads its own `x's back as literal text and runs away through the bank -- the screen fills with them and the run hits the frame cap with every needle here missing, SPSTART included.
command: /testbin/slogprobe; logger -p user.notice -t LGT 'a%sb' x y; sleep 2; grep LGT /usr/adm/messages
